_comment: Held-out test set and lures for the two-sequence-align chain. Serve one at a time, cold, days apart, mixed with other problems; never in sequence and never labelled as part of the chain.

3503.title: Longest Palindrome After Substring Concatenation I
3503.holds: run length of s[:i] against reversed t[:j]
3503.change: 718 on s and t[::-1], then add the longest palindrome that starts right after the run
3503.disguise: asks for a palindrome built from two substrings; no table in sight

3290.title: Maximum Multiplication Score
3290.holds: best score using a[:i] against b[:j]
3290.change: only b may skip, every a[i] must be used; a has exactly 4 entries
3290.disguise: a is fixed length 4, reads like pick 4 indices

1638.title: Count Substrings That Differ by One Character
1638.holds: run of equal characters ending at s[i-1], t[j-1] (and a second table for the run starting there)
1638.change: 718 table read from both ends; a mismatch cell scores (left run + 1) * (right run + 1)
1638.disguise: a counting question about substrings that differ in one place
sources: research/doocs-leetcode/solution/1600-1699/1638.Count Substrings That Differ by One Character/README_EN.md

3836.title: Maximum Score Using Exactly K Pairs
3836.holds: best score of exactly p pairs from nums1[:i], nums2[:j]
3836.change: a third index p counts the pairs; exactly k of them
3836.disguise: phrased as choosing index pairs with increasing i and j

3316.title: Find Maximum Removals From Source String
3316.holds: most removals in source[:i] while pattern[:j] is matched
3316.change: max instead of sum; up adds 1 when index i-1 is removable
3316.disguise: phrased as deleting indices while keeping a subsequence

1639.title: Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary
1639.holds: ways to form target[:i] using columns [:j]
1639.change: a match multiplies by how many words have that letter in column j
1639.disguise: a dictionary of words; the second sequence is the columns, not a string
sources: research/doocs-leetcode/solution/1600-1699/1639.Number of Ways to Form a Target String Given a Dictionary/README_EN.md

2430.title: Maximum Deletions on a String
2430.holds: length of the common prefix of s[i:] and s[j:]
2430.change: 718 suffix table on s against itself, then a 1D dp that reads it
2430.disguise: one string, a deletion game; the table is a helper

3981.title: Count Distinct Ways to Form Target from Two Strings
3981.holds: ways to form target[k:] from word1[i:] and word2[j:]
3981.change: 97 with counting (115) instead of bool; both strings may skip; each must be used once
3981.disguise: three strings and a count; reads like a combinatorics question

3388.title: Count Beautiful Splits in an Array
3388.holds: length of the common prefix of nums[i:] and nums[j:]
3388.change: 718 suffix table on nums against itself, then count splits with it
3388.disguise: one array, a split-counting question about prefixes

3983.title: Subsequence After One Replacement
3983.looks_like: s against t, subsequence with one change; reads like 115 or 72
3983.actually: greedy two pointers; one pointer with the replacement unused, one with it spent

214.title: Shortest Palindrome
214.looks_like: add characters to make a palindrome; reads like 1312 on s and s[::-1]
214.actually: longest palindromic prefix via KMP failure function on s + '#' + s[::-1] (or rolling hash); insertions only at the front

2800.title: Shortest String That Contains Three Strings
2800.looks_like: shortest string containing others; reads like 1092
2800.actually: substrings, not subsequences: try the 6 orders and merge by largest overlap

3472.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence After at Most K Operations
3472.looks_like: 516 plus a budget k; tempts s against s[::-1]
3472.actually: interval dp on one string, dfs(i, j, k) over s[i..j]; the reversed-copy table double counts the cost
sources: research/doocs-leetcode/solution/3400-3499/3472.Longest Palindromic Subsequence After at Most K Operations/README_EN.md

940.title: Distinct Subsequences II
940.actually: 1D dp over the last character, 26 counters

2193.title: Minimum Number of Moves to Make Palindrome
2193.looks_like: make a string a palindrome with fewest moves; reads like 1312
2193.actually: greedy: fix the outer pair, swap its match inward, count adjacent swaps
sources: research/doocs-leetcode/solution/2100-2199/2193.Minimum Number of Moves to Make Palindrome/README_EN.md
